evidence.api_compatibility: The router change (router.cpp) catches ConfigurationException separately and throws it without triggering the model eviction/retry path. This is not a breaking API change — the HTTP response shape is unchanged and the error is still returned to the client — but it changes the server's internal behavior around configuration errors, which could affect users relying on the previous retry behavior. The sd-cpp ROCm filename for Windows is new (sd-<version>-bin-win-rocm-<therock>-x64.zip) so it does not affect existing setups.
evidence.documentation: README and backends-reference were updated to list ROCm as supported on Windows and Linux (per the PR body). The validation script help text was updated to document the new --logs-dir requirement for GPU backends. The auto-generated CodeRabbit release notes summary is reasonable but imprecise — it does not mention the router configuration-error behavior change or the Windows path-length refusal.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The author reports testing on four Windows Strix Halo (gfx1151) machines and confirms GPU execution via server log lines. However, the new Windows MAX_PATH refusal path (when cache dir + install tree depth exceeds 259 characters) and the router configuration-error handling change (ConfigurationException now stops model loading without retry) have not been manually exercised in a release-candidate environment.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The final approval from @ramkrishna2910 was at 2026-10-19T06:44:09Z; the PR was merged via merge queue at 2026-10-19T08:11:03Z. The merge queue ran all CI checks which passed. No substantive post-approval behavior changes are evident from the review history — the author responded to all CodeRabbit suggestions and inline comments through the final approval.
evidence.review: Three reviewers with subject-matter expertise approved: @superm1 (ROCm) approved at 2026-10-01T18:10:59Z, @jeremyfowers (CI/infra) approved at 2026-10-02T19:27:28Z, @ramkrishna2910 (stable diffusion, ROCm) approved at 2026-10-19T06:44:09Z. @ramkrishna2910 provided the most thorough review, submitting inline comments that caught four bugs (path guard failing open, stale cached absolute path, missing _WIN32 guard, tests not exercising real code). All were addressed by the author. @jeremyfowers initially requested changes around GPU offload verification and was satisfied when the author added per-model GPU offload checks to the validation scripts. CodeRabbitAI also ran multiple reviews, suggesting fixes that were all addressed.
evidence.security: The commit stages DLLs (amdhip64* and amd_comgr*) into the sd-server executable directory. This is a Windows DLL hijacking mitigation — by staging TheRock's known-good runtime DLLs alongside the executable, it prevents System32's display driver DLLs from being loaded in a mixed pair. The staging logic only copies files that System32 would shadow or that already exist in the exe directory, so it is not introducing arbitrary copies. No supply-chain, credential, or telemetry changes.
evidence.tests: New file test/cpp/test_rocm_path_measure.cpp (193 lines) exercises BackendUtils::measure_rocblas_max_path and ensure_rocm_tensile_reachable directly with fixture trees at normal and excessive cache directory lengths, including a >260 character subdirectory case on Windows. New shared helper test/utils/gpu_offload.py is consumed by validate_llamacpp.py and validate_sdcpp.py. Both validation scripts now require --logs-dir for GPU backends and assert GPU device lines (e.g., "Initializing backend: ROCm0") appear in the server log. The CI workflow was updated to add rocm backend coverage for sd-cpp validation. No evidence of tests being weakened or deleted.

maintainer_todos.text: On a Windows machine with a Windows ROCm installation and an sd-cpp backend installed, start lemond with log_level=debug, load SD-Turbo with the rocm backend, and confirm the server log shows "Initializing backend: ROCm0" and the image generation completes in seconds rather than failing to the CPU.

On a Windows machine where LEMONADE_CACHE_DIR resolves to a path that, combined with the installed ROCm tree depth, exceeds 259 characters, start lemond and load any sd-cpp rocm model; confirm it fails with a ConfigurationException mentioning the cache directory length and that the error message suggests rocm_install_method=tarball.

Start lemond, load a model on the rocm backend, then attempt to load a second model with a deliberately invalid configuration; confirm the router throws the error immediately and the first loaded model remains active.

shout_outs.reason: Provided an exceptional inline review that caught four real bugs in the ROCm path guard: a scan error returning 0 (false pass that caused an access violation), a cached absolute path length that broke when a user moved their cache directory, a missing _WIN32 guard that would block Linux users, and a unit test that never called the real code. Each finding was reproduced with a specific scenario and the author addressed all four.

subject: Restore sdcpp rocm support on Windows (#3718)
summary: Re-enables the sd-cpp ROCm backend on Windows by staging the full HIP runtime DLL set (amdhip64* and amd_comgr*) into the sd-server executable directory instead of only amdhip64_7.dll, preventing a mixed-pair DLL loading bug that caused silent CPU fallback, and adds a Windows MAX_PATH guard for rocBLAS Tensile file lengths, router configuration-error handling, and GPU offload validation in CI.
verdict_reason: The PR introduces user-facing behavior changes (the Windows ROCm path-length refusal and the router configuration-error handling change) that have no evidence of being manually exercised on a release-candidate installation.
